Itikadi, umwinyi,
Usemi, Ubepari, Uchanganuzi Tahakiki
Usemi.
Itikadi ni mawazo na fikra zinazohalalisha masuala katika kijamii.
Fikra hizi huhalalisha mamlaka ya kisiasa na seti za matendo zinazotekeleza vitendo.
Itikadi hupata mamlaka na uhalali kwa hiari bila kutumia nguvu.
Viongozi wa kisiasa na kidini hujiegemeza katika itikadi fulani ili kufanikisha malengo yao kwa sababu wanafahamu kuwa itikadi hiyo imekubalika na wanajamii.
Mabadiliko hayawezi kuepukika, na jinsi sekta tofauti tofauti katika jamii zinapopitia mabadiliko ndivyo viongozi wanavyobadilisha mbinu za uongozi wao.
Pia, historia inapobadilika ndivyo itikadi inavyobadilika katika jamii.
Makala imeeleza dhana ya itikadi, imefafanua aina za itikadi na kuzibainisha katika tamthilia za Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004) na Kifo Kisimani (2001).
Baadhi ya aina za itikadi ambazo zimebainishwa katika tamthilia teule ni pamoja na; itikadi ya dini, ukombozi, utawala, itikadi ya utamaduni, itikadi ya umwinyi na itikadi ya ubepari.
Aina hizi zimebainishwa kutokana na usemi wa wahusika na muktadha mazungumzo.
Utafiti wa makala hii umeongozwa na nadharia ya Uchanganuzi Tahakiki Usemi (UTU) ilioasisiwa na Norman Fairclough (1989).
Nadharia hii hueleza uhusiano uliopo kati ya matukio ya kisiasa, kiusemi, kiutamaduni, kimatini na kijamii.
Huangazia athari ya itikadi katika matukio haya.
Pia, huangazia jinsi usemi huo huathiri matukio haya katika jamii.

NADHARIA
Itikadi ni dhana iliyo na maana nyingi.
Eagleton (1991) ametaja baadhi ya maelezo ya dhana ya itikadi kama; mchakato wa kuunda maana, ishara na maadili katika jamii.
Pili, itikadi ni mkusanyiko wa mawazo ya kundi fulani la kijamii au tabaka.
Tatu; itikadi ni mawazo au fikra ambazo huhalalisha mamlaka ya kisiasa na seti za matendo zinazotekeleza vitendo.
Eagleton (1991) anaendelea kueleza kuwa, itikadi hupata maana kutokana na mabadiliko ya kihistoria.
Marx na Engels (1977), wanaeleza itikadi kama fikra zote na maoni ya wanadamu kuhusu wanayosema na kufikiria kuhusu dini, sheria, siasa, uchumi na maadili.
Itikadi ndiyo huelekeza namna mtunzi anavyosawiri maudhui na dhamira yake.
Itikadi humwelekeza mwanadamu kuyatenda matendo mazuri au mabaya (Murithi, 2017).
Mtindo na mbinu za uandishi huwa na athari za kiitikadi kama anavyotaja Fairclough (2001).
Makala hii imeongozwa na nadharia ya Uchanganizi Tahakiki Usemi (UTU).
Nadharia ya UTU iliasisiwa na Fairclough Norman (1989) huko Lancaster School of Linguistics.
Waitifaki wa nadharia hii ni pamoja na Wodak (1997) na Dijk (1998).
Kwa mujibu wa Wodak (1997) UTU huangazia itikadi na utawala kutokana na data iliyoandikwa, inayoonekana, na iliyozungumzwa.
Kulingana na Wodak, UTU huchukulia lugha kama tendo la kijamii na kuona muktadha wa lugha kuwa muhimu sana.
Fairclough (2001) anaeleza kuwa UTU ni sayansi muhimu sana ya kijamii inayoangazia matatizo ambayo watu wanakumbana nayo kutokana na hali fulani ya maisha katika jamii na jinsi ya kuepuka matatizo hayo.
Anaendelea kueleza kuwa dhana ya usemi huongozwa na itikadi.
Mihimili ya UTU iliyoongoza utafiti wa makala hii ni; itikadi, utamaduni, usemi, viwango vya uchanganuzi na muundo wa jamii.
Mbinu ya Utafiti
Utafiti wa makala hii ulifanyiwa maktabani.
Watafiti walisoma tamthilia teule za Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi na Kifo Kisimani.
Pia, walisoma vitabu na kupekea makala mtandaoni yanayohusiana na malengo ya makala hii.
Dhana na aina za itikadi zimebainishwa kwa kujikita katika muundo wa kimaelezo.

MATOKEO NA MAJADILIANO YA UTAFITI
Katika sehemu hii, aina za itikadi zimefafanuliwa na kubainishwa kutoka katika tamthilia teule.
Aina za itikadi ambazo zimebainishwa katika tamthilia teule ni pamoja na; itikadi ya dini, ukombozi, utawala, itikadi ya utamaduni, itikadi ya umwinyi na itikadi ya ubepari.
Aina za itikadi zilizoainishwa ni kutokana na mawazo ya kijumla ya wataalam tofauti tofauti.
Itikadi ya Dini
Davis (1994) anaeleza dini kama mazoea ya kijamii.
Kwa hivyo, dini inaathiri jamii kwa kuweka vigezo vya kukihukumu kile ambacho wanadamu wanakifanya katika jamii.
Anaendelea kueleza kuwa, dini inasisitiza kuwa si kila jambo ambalo mwanadamu anafikiria na kutenda ni nzuri na lenye thamana.
Imani ya dini katika jamii huzua utata inapotafsiri masuala ya ulimwengu nje ya ufahamu wa kiroho.
Dini huonyesha kuwa utaratibu wa kijamii haukuanzishwa na binadamu bali kiumbe kilicho zaidi yake.
Imani hii hupitishwa kutoka kizazi kimoja hadi kingine kama sehemu ya utamaduni.
Davis (1994) anaonyesha matumizi ya lugha za kisiasa na matumizi mabaya ya lugha za kidini katika siasa.
Wanasiasa wanatumia mfumo wa dini unaowaongoza wanadamu kuwadhulumu.
Anatoa mfano wa Waisraeli ambao walitunukiwa ardhi takatifu na Mungu.
Walitumia imani ya kupewa ardhi na Mungu kuhalalisha matendo yao na hali zao hasa kwa Wapalestina.
Hata Waisraeli ambao hawakuwa wanathamini mambo ya Mungu, walitumia kigezo cha ‘kupewa ardhi na Mungu’ kwa sababu ya kujihalalisha.
Dini ina maana nyingi kutegemea mitazamo ya wataalamu mbalimbali.
Cosmstock (1984) anafafanua dini kama kile kilicho kitakatifu, uaminifu wa kuendeleza matendo mazuri, upendo kwa binadamu, na imani kwa miungu.
Anaendelea kueleza kuwa dini ni kile ambacho tunakitenda bila kuonekana na kuilinda jamii.
Aidha, Schilbrack (2013) anaeleza dini kama dhana inayotatua matatizo.
Lakini ni matatizo yepi yanayofafanua matendo ya kidini yanapotatuliwa?
Kwa mujibu wa Fitzgerald (2011), dini kwa jumla ni imani yenye sifa bia kuhusu uzoefu wa binadamu na taasisi.
Anachukulia dini kama masuala ya kiroho na ‘ulimwengu mwingine’.
Ni imani katika nguvu zisizo za kawaida.
Dini ni upendo, amani, isiyopenda vurugu na isiyojihusisha na siasa.
Fitzgerald anataja baadhi ya aina za dini kama dini ya Ukristo, Uhindu, Uislamu, na Ubudhi.
Dini hizi zinaongozwa na itikadi tofauti tofauti.
Kutokana na maelezo ya wataalam mbalimbali, dini ni mazoea ya kijamii yanayoyahusisha masuala ya kiroho na imani katika kiumbe kilicho zaidi ya binadamu.
Matendo ya binadamu huongozwa na imani walionayo kwa kiumbe kilicho zaidi yao.
Katika tamthilia ya Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004) suala la dini linadhihirika kutokana na muktadha wa mazungumzo kati ya Nyagachi, Kabitho, na Gachono (uk.

Wakombozi wanaamini katika suala la kuleta haki katika malipo ya mshahara na kupewa nafasi sawa katika masuala yote ya kijamii pasi kudhulimiwa na viongozi wao.
Plamenatz (1970), Davis (1994), na Cavanaugh (2009) wanachukulia itikadi ya dini kama imani inayotumiwa kuwapotosha wanadamu.
Utaratibu wa kijamii ulioanzishwa na kiumbe kilicho zaidi ya binadamu unatumiwa kuficha tabia za ndani za binadamu na kumfanya kuamini kuwa yeye ni mwathiriwa wa mambo yaliyo zaidi ya uwezo wake.
Mwelekeo wa mtunzi wa tamthilia za Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi na Kifo Kisimani unaoana na mawazo ya Plamenatz, Davis, na Cavanaugh kwa namna anavyosawiri imani ya wahusika kutokana na; muktadha wa mazungumzo na usemi unaoongozwa na itikadi.
Mtunzi anaonyesha namna wahusika wanavyoendeleza vurugu na kuwakandamiza wenzao kwa misingi ya itikadi ya dini.
Mwelekeo wa mtunzi ni kuwa dini inatumika kuendeleza uongozi mbaya na kuwapotosha wanajamii kutojikomboa kutoka kwa dhuluma.
Kwa mujibu wa Eddins (1972), ukombozi ni itikadi ya kisiasa ambayo inatoa mwongozo wa kuziunda sera za umma.
Wakombozi wanaamini kuwa lengo kuu la sera za umma ni kuzilinda haki za wanaodhulumiwa na kuhakikisha usawa wa kukua na kujiendeleza kikamilifu.
Aidha, Gramsci (1994) anaeleza kuwa ni vigumu kupata ukombozi.
Wanaohitaji kukombolewa wamepewa majukumu na jamii kwa ‘manufaa ya wote’.
Wamezoea majukumu haya na kuyaona ya kawaida.
Gramsci anaendelea kueleza kuwa wanajamii wanahitaji kufahamu na kuelewa nafasi yao katika historia, haki zao na wajibu wao.
Anasisitiza umuhimu wa elimu katika kufikia ukombozi na haja ya elimu ya demokrasia.
Kwake, elimu inawezesha jamii kidhibiti nguvu zinazowatawala na kupata ukombozi japokuwa itachukua muda mrefu kupata ukombozi.

Kulingana na maoni ya Montero (2009), ukombozi ni mchakato unaohusisha mabadiliko ya kijamii kwa lengo la kuleta usawa, kupinga ukandamizaji na dhuluma.

Key Terms:

discourse analysis. Ideology refers to ideas and beliefs that legitimize social issues. These beliefs legitimize political authority and the sets of actions that carry out practices. Ideology gains authority and legitimacy voluntarily without the use of force. Political and religious leaders align themselves with certain ideologies to achieve their goals because they understand that these ideologies are accepted by members of society. Change is inevitable, and as different sectors in society undergo change, leaders also adapt their leadership approaches. Likewise, as history changes, ideology also shifts within society. The article has explained the concept of ideology, clarified the types of ideology, and identified them in the plays Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004) and Kifo Kisimani (2001). Some of the types of ideology identified in the selected plays include religious ideology, liberation ideology, governance ideology, cultural ideology, feudal ideology, and capitalist ideology. These types have been identified through the discourse of characters and the context of their conversations. The research in this article is guided by the Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) theory established by Norman Fairclough (1989). This theory explains the relationship that exists between political, discursive, cultural, textual, and social events. It highlights the impact of ideology in these events. THEORY  
Ideology is a concept with many meanings. Eagleton (1991) has listed some descriptions of the concept of ideology as: the process of creating meaning, symbols, and values in society. Second, ideology is a collection of ideas held by a particular social group or class. Third, ideology consists of ideas or beliefs that legitimize political authority and the sets of actions that carry out practices. Eagleton (1991) further explains that ideology derives its meaning from historical changes. Marx and Engels (1977) define ideology as all human ideas and views regarding what they say and think about religion, law, politics, economics, and morals. Ideology guides how an author depicts themes and their intention. Ideology directs a person to perform good or bad actions (Murithi, 2017). Writing styles and methods have ideological effects, as noted by Fairclough (2001). This article is guided by the theory of Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA). The CDA theory was founded by Norman Fairclough (1989) at the Lancaster School of Linguistics. Key proponents of this theory include Wodak (1997) and Dijk (1998). According to Wodak (1997), CDA focuses on ideology and governance based on written, visual, and spoken data. Wodak states that CDA regards language as a social act and considers the context of language to be very important. Fairclough (2001) explains that CDA is a crucial social science that examines the problems people face due to specific social circumstances and how to avoid those problems. He further explains that the concept of discourse is guided by ideology. The use of drums in the context of their conversations ...how are things on the side of the drums? tax. Holton (1985) states that feudalism is not a mode of production but a means of promoting cohesion within society. He goes on to explain that the feudal system has a well-structured arrangement for farmers and is not about oppression and land ownership as it is commonly perceived. Kaloo: Today, there are words; hips will be shaken until they melt. Batu: Like fuel? Kaloo: Like fuel near a fire. Batu: Fuel! Then let the waists and hips melt! Which dance will you play? Kaloo: Several. One of them is chakacha (i.e. 3-4). Wamitila (2003) describes feudalism as an economic system in which the wealthy inherit their wealth while owning large estates along with political power. According to Hilton (1983), feudalism represents a social structure in which rulers use power to gain authority. Therefore, the methods used by feudal lords to oppress peasants stem from political reasons rather than building the economy. From this discussion, the beliefs of the characters Batu and Kaloo regarding their ideology become evident. They believe in a dance tradition that involves shaking the hips with the aim of entertaining the Chief. Moreover, the issue of dance tradition is also evident through Gege, who uses expressions that reflect his beliefs about dance. On page 44, he explains the activities he undertakes to build his reputation in dance. Martin (1986) defines feudalism on social and economic grounds to explain the relationship that existed between graduates who worked on plantations and the owners of those plantations. It is a system in which the workers produce goods, but their produce is taken by the landlords. Martin explains that, in this system, the workers who produce goods are separated from those products. The landlords are the ones who control the amount of land used by the workers and all payment methods by charging high fees. The playwright's approach in the selected play is that culture is used to achieve the goals of leaders or individuals, as evidenced by the way he portrays characters and how they use language in conversational contexts. He focuses on how the life experiences of certain people (Wamitila, 2003) are used by leaders to oppress members of the community. For example, the culture of songs praising good governance contrasts with the actual reality. According to various experts, the ideology of Umwinyi is a system in which the wealthy own and control large estates. Graduates are used by these wealthy individuals to generate wealth but are separated from their produce by being allocated limited land they are allowed to use and being charged high taxes and fees. The ideology of feudalism. In the play Mau in the Morning Sun (2004), Kabitho claims to defend the rights of his fellow Wandiku while in reality perpetuating a feudal system. Why is it that Wandiku and his companions have no homes while he owns vast lands? They sleep on the cold ground and their children die, yet Kabitho is unaware of these deaths. The social structure has created class barriers where the upper class  
According to Holton (1985), the concept of feudalism was used in Europe from the 16th century onwards. It was used to refer to the ownership of cattle. He goes on to explain that the ideology of feudalism was perpetuated by powerful people who owned land. The landowners exploited the peasants by charging them taxes and Kabitho's family owns more than one hundred and fifty acres of land, while the lower class represented by people like Nyagachi are landless and are squatters. As evident in the conversation between Kabitho and Tungai:
Kabitho: How are they? They are all at the Buratu farm. They have gone to oversee the harvesting of potatoes and pyrethrum. I am the only one left here. Tungai: What have you planted here? In the play Kifo Kisimani (2001), the writer portrays the ideology of feudalism through the character of Mtemi Bokono. Additionally, he also depicts those who oppose this system through the character Nyalwe. As mentioned earlier, the social structure examines social constraints such as class, rank, and status. From this perspective, we recognize how rank and status are used to perpetuate the feudal system. The characters have been assigned titles such as Chief Soldier and Land Distributor as mentioned by Nyalwe. The Land Distributor perpetuates the system of feudalism by allocating to the Chief Soldier the land belonging to the villagers, represented by Mama Agoro, as is evident:
Kabitho: Wheat in one hundred and fifty acres. In the remaining section I have planted crops (p. 7). Nyalwe: What I am saying is important. Do not mock me! Mama Agoro came to complain. She says the playground for their children has been taken away. You have been given the Chief of Security. Bokono: Who appointed the Chief of Security? Nyalwe: Land Allocator. To highlight the feudal system promoted by Kabitho. From the conversations between Nyagachi, Kabitho, and Gachono, we recognize the adverse effects of this system. Nyagachi explains how they were evicted from their farms. She asks Kabitho whether visiting them will help return their land. Defending his beliefs, Kabitho explains that they are making plans to return their land. Bokono: So why did he come here instead of going to the land distributor?  
Nyalwe: When officials ignore the regulations governing their authority, their superior must be reminded to observe those rules.  
Bokono: Which regulations has the land distributor ignored?  
Nyalwe: The regulations that protect public land. The conversation between Nali, Nche, and Chebwe reveals how deeply rooted feudalism is. Those with large tracts of land do not use it to build the economy, while their counterparts do not even have ten feet. The social structure has led to the creation of the saying "maskuota," which reflects class divisions. Nali uses the term maskuota to refer to those who live on land that does not belong to them without the permission of the landowner, as illustrated:
Nali: Father, there are many Wandiku who do not even have a single acre…
The context of the conversation between Bokono and Nyalwe points to the ideology of feudalism promoted by characters tasked with defending the principles of protecting public land. As Holton (previously mentioned) explains, the feudal system is perpetuated by powerful individuals who oppress people from lower classes. Nali; …. A few people have thousands of acres while others do not even have ten square feet of land. Some of these major landowners do not use it to contribute to the country’s economy… We have many squatters (pp. 60-61). In the way the author portrays the characters, the selected playwright has demonstrated their perspective. Regarding characters who possess power and authority, the selected playwright depicts them as owning large farms and wielding political influence. Their beliefs about the feudal system reflect a social structure that grants rulers inherited authority and control over land, while community members are left landless. The ideology of capitalism permeates all social, economic, and political spheres. Furthermore, this system not only connects people within a single nation but also links the entire world. Based on this explanation, the ideology of capitalism involves an economic, social, and political system owned by a few individuals for their personal benefit. Capitalists are guided by the belief in using graduates in the production process, but they are not involved in the benefits of the products of their production. Graduates are unable to advance economically due to strict regulations imposed by capitalists in all economic and political sectors. Capitalism involves an economic system. Murithi (2017) describes the economy as the sum of all human activities aimed at satisfying people's needs. The economic system involves the production, distribution, consumption of goods, and the provision of various services. The capitalist system emerged from the feudal system according to Marx’s ideas (1941). Furthermore, Anderson (1979) disputes the claim that feudalism is the origin of capitalism. Anderson considers capitalism as a system involving economic development resulting from the expansion of certain methods of production. According to Holton (1985), the emergence of capitalist modes of production and their growth during the industrial era depended on previously existing methods. He goes on to explain that capitalism is not a sign of economic freedom but rather a sign of exploitation and a struggle for power in the sphere of production. Capitalism is an economic, political, and social system characterized by private ownership of property, business, and industry with the aim of generating substantial profits for the benefit of certain individuals. Capitalists use graduates to serve their own interests. Laclau (1979) states that capitalism involves the following: a system of production for the market, profit as the driving force of production, and finally, this profit is realized for the benefit of someone other than the producer. In the play Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004), from the conversations between Gachono, Nyagachi, and Kabitho, we perceive how the economy has deteriorated. Considering the levels of analysis that highlight the context of social relationships which affect speech, expressions that indicate the poor state of the lower class are used. The presence of fleas, food shortages, and the deaths of women and children are the result of certain individuals accumulating public wealth for themselves. On page 2, Nyagachi explains that they were evicted from their farms. They do not have title deeds to their land because they were destroyed by fires. It is customary to have a land ownership title as proof that the land belongs to a particular person. They believe that if they do not have those titles, it will be difficult to reclaim the land that was taken from them, as is evident:

Gachono: Look at the shacks where we sleep. Look at the black plastic sheets with large holes like the mouths of caves.  
Amin (2011) describes capitalism as the absence of equality resulting from political, economic, and social relationships. He identifies the capitalist system as the opposite of the governing relationship between political, social, and economic entities. This lack of equality leads to the emergence of new markets dominated by capitalists who control social production and impose high taxes. Amin (2011) goes on to explain that the capitalists, who make up 20%, need the graduates, who constitute 80%, to benefit themselves because of

Gachono: …. Bitter cold. Cold that burns like fire. Nyagachi: Children are dying from pneumonia. And yet the graves have not closed their doors. 2-3). of society, Gege describes him as someone who, instead of thinking about ways to enrich himself and enjoy life, is preoccupied with thinking about society. From Gege’s statements, it is clear that he believes in accumulating wealth and advancing oneself economically without caring for others. Gachono uses simile to emphasize the condition of the Wandiku who were evicted from their land. For example: the cold that burns like fire. They compare this situation to demonstrate its severity, as is evident in the intense language in the above conversation. Furthermore, this situation aligns with Amin's (2011) view that the capitalist system hinders human civilization. The perspective of the playwright of Kifo Kisimani and Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004) regarding the ideology of capitalism points to individual economic, social, and political advancement (Holton, 1985). The playwright has demonstrated a negative attitude towards the capitalist system based on the way he uses language to emphasize the selfishness of some characters in their personal advancement. Capitalists do not care about the interests of others, only their own. They are driven by the profits obtained from the production and distribution of goods and services. The author has shown how members of society are affected by this system that hinders human civilization (Amin, 2011). CONCLUSION
The economic and social system should benefit all members of society. Moreover, in the play Kifo Kisimani, the opposite is true. The capitalists benefit from all social, economic, and political streams (Amin, 2011). Discourse is a social act (Dijk, 1993); from Andua's utterance, we recognize how the ideology of capitalism is perpetuated. The villagers are not allowed to fetch water from the Mkuyuni well. Based on the conversation between Andua and Tanya (UK 49), it becomes evident that the water from the reservoir, which should be used for human benefit, has been left for the chief’s son’s cattle. Instead of fetching water for the cattle, they are released inside so they can drink directly from the reservoir. Andua explains how the guards beat them because they fetched water from the well, and one of them pushed him, causing him to fall onto a stone and get injured. In this article, the concept of ideology is defined as all the thoughts and opinions of human beings regarding what they say and think about political, social, and economic issues. The types of ideologies have been identified in the plays Kifo Kisimani (2001) and Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004). Some of the types of ideology identified are religious, governance, cultural, feudal, capitalist, and liberation ideologies. Researchers have demonstrated the types of ideology by focusing on the context of conversations, speech, content, and the relationships that exist between characters. Beliefs in society about living conditions are manifested in the speech of characters. Speech is a type of social act. In the play “Kifo Kisimani” (2001), Gege’s speech signifies a social act of amassing wealth without caring for others. His speech aligns with Anderson’s (1979) ideas, who explains that capitalism involves personal advancement in economic, political, and social spheres. NADHARIA
Itikadi ni dhana iliyo na maana nyingi. Eagleton (1991) ametaja baadhi ya maelezo ya dhana ya itikadi kama; mchakato wa kuunda maana, ishara na maadili katika jamii. Pili, itikadi ni mkusanyiko wa mawazo ya kundi fulani la kijamii au tabaka. Tatu; itikadi ni mawazo au fikra ambazo huhalalisha mamlaka ya kisiasa na seti za matendo zinazotekeleza vitendo. Eagleton (1991) anaendelea kueleza kuwa, itikadi hupata maana kutokana na mabadiliko ya kihistoria. Marx na Engels (1977), wanaeleza itikadi kama fikra zote na maoni ya wanadamu kuhusu wanayosema na kufikiria kuhusu dini, sheria, siasa, uchumi na maadili. Itikadi ndiyo huelekeza namna mtunzi anavyosawiri maudhui na dhamira yake. Itikadi humwelekeza mwanadamu kuyatenda matendo mazuri au mabaya (Murithi, 2017). Mtindo na mbinu za uandishi huwa na athari za kiitikadi kama anavyotaja Fairclough (2001).

INTRODUCTION  
Cultural ideology, feudal ideology, and capitalist ideology  
THEORY  
Ideology is a concept with many meanings. Eagleton (1991) has listed some descriptions of the concept of ideology as: the process of creating meaning, symbols, and values in society. Second, ideology is a collection of ideas held by a particular social group or class. Third, ideology consists of ideas or beliefs that legitimize political authority and the sets of actions that carry out practices. Eagleton (1991) further explains that ideology derives its meaning from historical changes. Marx and Engels (1977) define ideology as all human ideas and views regarding what they say and think about religion, law, politics, economics, and morals. Ideology guides how an author depicts themes and their intention. Ideology directs a person to perform good or bad actions (Murithi, 2017). Writing styles and methods have ideological effects, as noted by Fairclough (2001).

discourses.source_txt: Makala hii imeongozwa na nadharia ya Uchanganizi Tahakiki Usemi (UTU). Nadharia ya UTU iliasisiwa na Fairclough Norman (1989) huko Lancaster School of Linguistics. Waitifaki wa nadharia hii ni pamoja na Wodak (1997) na Dijk (1998). Kwa mujibu wa Wodak (1997) UTU huangazia itikadi na utawala kutokana na data iliyoandikwa, inayoonekana, na iliyozungumzwa. Kulingana na Wodak, UTU huchukulia lugha kama tendo la kijamii na kuona muktadha wa lugha kuwa muhimu sana. Fairclough (2001) anaeleza kuwa UTU ni sayansi muhimu sana ya kijamii inayoangazia matatizo ambayo watu wanakumbana nayo kutokana na hali fulani ya maisha katika jamii na jinsi ya kuepuka matatizo hayo.
discourses.translated_txt: This article is guided by the theory of Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA). The CDA theory was founded by Norman Fairclough (1989) at the Lancaster School of Linguistics. Key proponents of this theory include Wodak (1997) and Dijk (1998). According to Wodak (1997), CDA focuses on ideology and governance based on written, visual, and spoken data. Wodak states that CDA regards language as a social act and considers the context of language to be very important. Fairclough (2001) explains that CDA is a crucial social science that examines the problems people face due to specific social circumstances and how to avoid those problems.

RESEARCH FINDINGS AND DISCUSSION  
In this section, the types of ideology are clarified and identified from the selected plays. The types of ideology identified in the selected plays include: religious ideology, liberation, governance, cultural ideology, feudal ideology, and capitalist ideology. The types of ideology listed are based on the general ideas of various scholars.  

Religious Ideology  
Davis (1994) describes religion as a social practice. Therefore, religion influences society by setting criteria for judging what humans do within society. He further explains that religion emphasizes that not everything a human thinks and does is good and valuable. Religious beliefs in society create controversy when interpreting worldly matters outside the realm of spiritual understanding. Religion shows that the social order was not established by humans, but by a being beyond them. This belief is passed down from one generation to another as part of culture.

Kulingana na maoni ya Montero (2009), ukombozi ni mchakato unaohusisha mabadiliko ya kijamii kwa lengo la kuleta usawa, kupinga ukandamizaji na dhuluma. Pia ukombozi huondoa taasisi zinazoendeleza maovu haya.
discourses.translated_txt:
Liberation Ideology  
According to Montero (2009), liberation is a process that involves social transformation aimed at promoting equality, opposing oppression and injustice. Liberation also eliminates institutions that perpetuate these evils.

discourses.source_txt: Ukombozi unanuia kuwahamasisha watu kuhusu haki zao na umuhimu wa kuishi katika jamii yenye usawa na demokrasia. Kutokana na maana tofauti tofauti za dhana ya itikadi ya ukombozi, ni dhahiri kuwa ukombozi unashughulikia haki za watu waliodhulumiwa na viongozi wao. Lengo la ukombozi ni kuwapa uhuru na uwezo wa kujiendeleza katika masuala yote ya kimaisha. Itikadi ya ukombozi inashikilia imani ya kujikomboa kutoka kwa uongozi mbaya. Kundi linaloshikilia imani hii linautekeleza mchakato huu kwa kuendeleza mapinduzi dhidi ya uongozi mbaya.
discourses.translated_txt: Liberation aims to raise people's awareness of their rights and the importance of living in an equal and democratic society. Given the various interpretations of the concept of the ideology of liberation, it is clear that liberation addresses the rights of people who have been oppressed by their leaders. The goal of liberation is to give them freedom and the ability to advance themselves in all aspects of life. The ideology of liberation upholds the belief in freeing oneself from bad leadership. Groups that adhere to this belief implement this process by advancing revolutions against poor leadership.

discourses.source_txt: Mwelekeo wa mtunzi wa tamthilia za Kifo Kisimani (2001) na Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004) ni kuwa jamii inafaa kujikomboa kutokana na ukatili na ukandamizwaji. Kutokana na maudhui na matumizi ya usemi katika muktadha wa mazungumzo kati ya wahusika, mtunzi ameonyesha namna vijana wako katika mstari wa mbele katika kuendeleza mchakato wa kupata ukombozi. Mwelekeo wa mtunzi katika tamthilia teule unaoana na mawazo ya Montero (2009), Pavkovic (2005), na Eddins (1972) ambao wanashikilia kuwa itikadi ya ukombozi ni hatua ya kuleta usawa, kukomboa kundi linalokandamizwa na kudhulumiwa na kuunda sera zinazolinda haki za umma.
discourses.translated_txt: The orientation of the playwright in the dramas *Kifo Kisimani* (2001) and *Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi* (2004) is that society should liberate itself from cruelty and oppression. Based on the themes and the use of expression in the context of dialogues between characters, the playwright has demonstrated how young people are at the forefront of advancing the process of achieving liberation. The perspective of the playwright in the selected plays aligns with the views of Montero (2009), Pavkovic (2005), and Eddins (1972), who maintain that the ideology of liberation is a step towards achieving equality, emancipating oppressed and marginalized groups, and formulating policies that protect public rights.

discourses.translated_txt: It is a system that establishes principles for the protection of rights and has responsibilities to ensure that the management of all societal affairs is effective. They go on to explain that it is important for the governance system to address all levels of society, politics, and the economy. Based on the various definitions of the concept of governance, it is clear that governance ideology involves the exercise of authority to improve and strengthen all social, political, and economic spheres. Leaders are required to promote good governance that advocates for and protects the rights of community members and ensures equity in the distribution of community resources.

discourses.translated_txt: Bokono is the ruler of Butangi, assisted by Batu and Zigu. The methods they use in their governance oppress the people of Butangi, as is evident in their conversations. Their dialogues have revealed how social relations and governance are manifested in their discourse (Dijk, 2001).

discourses.translated_txt: Kithaka wa Mberia has demonstrated his perspective on the ideology of governance through the discourse and context of dialogues among characters in the plays Kifo Kisimani (2001) and Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004). His perspective is that rulers seek to maintain their leadership without regard for the interests of the community. He focuses on showing how rulers use laws to perpetuate the ideology of governance rather than to protect rights (Althusser, 1981).

discourses.translated_txt: Martin (1986) defines feudalism on social and economic grounds to explain the relationship that existed between graduates who worked on plantations and the owners of those plantations.

discourses.translated_txt: The playwright's approach in the selected play is that culture is used to achieve the goals of leaders or individuals, as evidenced by the way he portrays characters and how they use language in conversational contexts. He focuses on how the life experiences of certain people (Wamitila, 2003) are used by leaders to oppress members of the community.

discourses.translated_txt: For example, the culture of songs praising good governance contrasts with the actual reality. According to various experts, the ideology of Umwinyi is a system in which the wealthy own and control large estates.

discourses.source_txt: Aidha, mfumo huu hauunganishi tu watu wa taifa moja bali ni mfumo unaounganisha ulimwengu. Kutokana na maelezo haya, itikadi ya ubepari inahusisha mfumo wa uzalishaji wa kiuchumi, kijamii, na kisiasa unaomilikiwa na watu wachache kwa manufaa yao binafsi.
discourses.translated_txt: Furthermore, this system not only connects people within a single nation but also links the entire world. Based on this explanation, the ideology of capitalism involves an economic, social, and political system owned by a few individuals for their personal benefit.

discourses.source_txt: Mabepari wanaongozwa na imani ya kutumia mahafali katika mchakato wa uzalishaji lakini hawahusishwi na faida ya mazao ya uzalishaji wao.
discourses.translated_txt: Capitalists are guided by the belief in using graduates in the production process, but they are not involved in the benefits of the products of their production.

discourses.source_txt: Mahafali hawana uwezo wa kujiendeleza kiuchumi kutokana na sheria kali zilizowekwa na mabepari katika mikondo yote ya kiuchumi na kisiasa.Ubepari unahusisha mfumo wa kiuchumi.
discourses.translated_txt: Graduates are unable to advance economically due to strict regulations imposed by capitalists in all economic and political sectors. Capitalism involves an economic system.

discourses.source_txt: Murithi (2017) anaeleza uchumi kama jumla ya shughuli zote za binadamu zinazolenga kutosheleza mahitaji ya watu.
discourses.translated_txt: Murithi (2017) describes the economy as the sum of all human activities aimed at satisfying people's needs.

discourses.source_txt: Mfumo wa kiuchumi unahusisha uzalishaji, usambazaji, utumiaji wa bidhaa na kutolewa kwa huduma mbalimbali.
discourses.translated_txt: The economic system involves the production, distribution, consumption of goods, and the provision of various services.

discourses.source_txt: Mfumo wa ubepari uliibuka kutokana na mfumo wa umwinyi kulingana na mawazo ya Marx (1941).
discourses.translated_txt: The capitalist system emerged from the feudal system according to Marx’s ideas (1941).

discourses.source_txt: Aidha, Anderson (1979) anapinga kauli kuwa umwinyi ndicho chanzo cha ubepari. Anderson anachukulia ubepari kama mfumo unaohusisha maendeleo ya kiuchumi kutokana na sifa za kupanuka kwa mbinu fulani ya uzalishaji.
discourses.translated_txt: Furthermore, Anderson (1979) disputes the claim that feudalism is the origin of capitalism. Anderson considers capitalism as a system involving economic development resulting from the expansion of certain methods of production.

discourses.source_txt: Kulingana na Holton (1985), kuibuka kwa mbinu za uzalishaji za kibepari na kukua kwake katika enzi za viwanda, kulitegemea mbinu zilizokuwepo awali.
discourses.translated_txt: According to Holton (1985), the emergence of capitalist modes of production and their growth during the industrial era depended on previously existing methods.

discourses.source_txt: Anaendelea kueleza kuwa ubepari si ishara ya uhuru wa kiuchumi bali ni ishara ya unyonyaji na mzozo wa kimadaraka katika nyanja ya uzalishaji. Ubepari ni mfumo wa kiuchumi, kisiasa na kijamii wa umiliki binafsi wa mali, biashara na viwanda kwa lengo la kutengeneza faida kubwa na baadhi ya watu binafsi kufaidika. Mabepari hutumia mahafali kujifaidi.
discourses.translated_txt: He goes on to explain that capitalism is not a sign of economic freedom but rather a sign of exploitation and a struggle for power in the sphere of production. Capitalism is an economic, political, and social system characterized by private ownership of property, business, and industry with the aim of generating substantial profits for the benefit of certain individuals. Capitalists use graduates to serve their own interests.

discourses.source_txt: Laclau (1979), anataja kuwa ubepari unahusisha mambo yafuatayo; mfumo wa uzalishaji kwa soko, faida ndicho kichocheo cha uzalishaji na mwisho, faida hii hupatikana kwa manufaa ya mtu mwingine ila si mzalishaji.
discourses.translated_txt: Laclau (1979) states that capitalism involves the following: a system of production for the market, profit as the driving force of production, and finally, this profit is realized for the benefit of someone other than the producer.

discourses.source_txt: Gachono anatumia tashbihi kusisitiza hali ya Wandiku waliofukuzwa kutoka kwa ardhi yao. Kwa mfano; baridi inayochoma kama moto. Wanailinganisha hali hiyo kuonyesha uzito wake kama inavyodhihirika katika maneno yaliyokolezwa katika mazungumzo ya hapo juu.
discourses.translated_txt: Gachono uses simile to emphasize the condition of the Wandiku who were evicted from their land. For example: the cold that burns like fire. They compare this situation to demonstrate its severity, as is evident in the intense language in the above conversation.

discourses.source_txt: Aidha, hali hii inaoana na mawazo ya Amin (2011) kuwa mfumo wa ubepari unazuia ustaarabu wa binadamu.
discourses.translated_txt: Furthermore, this situation aligns with Amin's (2011) view that the capitalist system hinders human civilization.

discourses.source_txt: Mwelekeo wa mtunzi wa tamthilia za Kifo Kisimani na Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004) kuhusu itikadi ya ubepari unaashiria maendeleo binafsi ya kiuchumi, kijamii na kisiasa, (Holton, 1985). Mtunzi amedhihirisha mwelekeo hasi kuhusu mfumo wa ubepari kutokana na namna alivyo tumia usemi kusisitiza ubinafsi wa baadhi ya wahusika katika kujiendeleza.
discourses.translated_txt: The perspective of the playwright of Kifo Kisimani and Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004) regarding the ideology of capitalism points to individual economic, social, and political advancement (Holton, 1985). The playwright has demonstrated a negative attitude towards the capitalist system based on the way he uses language to emphasize the selfishness of some characters in their personal advancement.

discourses.source_txt: Mabepari hawajali maslahi ya watu wengine bali yao tu. Wanachochewa na faida zinazotokana na uzalishaji na usambazaji wa bidhaa na huduma.
discourses.translated_txt: Capitalists do not care about the interests of others, only their own. They are driven by the profits obtained from the production and distribution of goods and services.

discourses.translated_txt: The author has shown how members of society are affected by this system that hinders human civilization (Amin, 2011).

discourses.translated_txt: Moreover, in the play Kifo Kisimani, the opposite is true. The capitalists benefit from all social, economic, and political streams (Amin, 2011).

discourses.translated_txt: Discourse is a social act (Dijk, 1993); from Andua's utterance, we recognize how the ideology of capitalism is perpetuated.

discourses.source_txt: Wanakijiji hawaruhusiwi kuchota maji kwenye kisima cha Mkuyuni.
discourses.translated_txt: The villagers are not allowed to fetch water from the Mkuyuni well.

discourses.source_txt: Kutokana na mazungumzo kati ya Andua na Tanya (UK 49), inadhihirika kuwa, maji ya bwawa ambayo yanafaa kutumika kwa manufaa ya wanadamu, yameachiwa ng’ombe wa mwanawe Mtemi.
discourses.translated_txt: Based on the conversation between Andua and Tanya (UK 49), it becomes evident that the water from the reservoir, which should be used for human benefit, has been left for the chief’s son’s cattle.

discourses.source_txt: Badala ya ngombe wale kuchotewa maji, wanaachiliwa ndani ili wanywe moja kwa moja kutoka bwawani. Andua anaeleza jinsi askari waliwapiga kwa sababu ya kuchota maji kisimani mmoja wao akamsukuma na kuangukia jiwe akaumia.
discourses.translated_txt: Instead of fetching water for the cattle, they are released inside so they can drink directly from the reservoir. Andua explains how the guards beat them because they fetched water from the well, and one of them pushed him, causing him to fall onto a stone and get injured.

discourses.source_txt: Katika makala hii, dhana ya itikadi imefafanuliwa kama fikra zote na maoni ya wanadamu kuhusu wanayosema na kuyafikiria kuhusu masuala ya kisiasa, kijamii na kiuchumi. Aina za itikadi zimebainishwa katika tamthilia za Kifo Kisimani (2001) na Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004).
discourses.translated_txt: In this article, the concept of ideology is defined as all the thoughts and opinions of human beings regarding what they say and think about political, social, and economic issues. The types of ideologies have been identified in the plays Kifo Kisimani (2001) and Maua kwenye Jua la Asubuhi (2004).

discourses.source_txt: Baadhi ya aina za itikadi zilizobainishwa ni itikadi ya dini, utawala, utamaduni, umwinyi, ubepari na ukombozi. Watafiti wameonyesha aina za itikadi kwa kujikita katika muktadha wa mazungumzo, usemi, maudhui na uhusiano uliopo kati ya wahusika.
discourses.translated_txt: Some of the types of ideology identified are religious, governance, cultural, feudal, capitalist, and liberation ideologies. Researchers have demonstrated the types of ideology by focusing on the context of conversations, speech, content, and the relationships that exist between characters.

discourses.source_txt: Imani katika jamii kuhusu hali ya maisha inadhihirika katika usemi wa wahusika. Usemi ni aina ya tendo la kijamii. Katika tamthilia ya Kifo Kisimani (2001) usemi wa Gege unaashiria tendo la kijamii la kujilimbikizia mali bila kuwajali wengine.
discourses.translated_txt: Beliefs in society about living conditions are manifested in the speech of characters. Speech is a type of social act. In the play “Kifo Kisimani” (2001), Gege’s speech signifies a social act of amassing wealth without caring for others.

discourses.source_txt: Usemi wake unaingiliana na mawazo ya Anderson (1979) anayeeleza kuwa ubepari unahusisha maendeleo binafsi ya kiuchumi, kisiasa na kijamii.
discourses.translated_txt: His speech aligns with Anderson’s (1979) ideas, who explains that capitalism involves personal advancement in economic, political, and social spheres.
